pipeline_name: Ameriya Cement-Borg El Arab Gas Pipeline

validity.recommendation: No change. Optionally attach the two Amreyah Cement corroboration URLs alongside the existing EGAS-2018 ref to document the endpoint verification.
validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE + SPEC (the sheet's own cited source, read as a MAP not full text): the current ref (EGAS/GASCO Annual Report 2017/2018) is a 36-page PDF. Printed page 35 (PDF page index 19) is the GASCO 'National Gas Grid' wall map. I downloaded the PDF and extracted the map image at native resolution (1811x2001, pdfimages object 2) rather than relying on text extraction, per this cohort's known pattern of visually-sourced rows. Zoomed 5x on the Alexandria/Western Desert Gas Complex (W.D.G. Complex) area west of Alexandria: the map shows a green 'Consumer' node labeled 'Ameriya Cement' and a blue 'Distribution' node labeled 'Borg Elarab' connected by a short green line (legend: green = 'EXISTING P/L'), with an attached leader-line label reading '12" 14km'. This is an EXACT match to GEM's Diameter=12in, LengthKnown=14.00km, and confirms Status=operating (green = existing, not the red 'under cons.' or blue-dashed 'under study' styles used elsewhere on the same map). This resolves url_verifier's automated flag on the Status ref ('operating' not found in extracted text) -- the map artwork isn't machine-readable text, so a text-search miss here is not evidence of a bad citation, consistent with the scope brief. Re-ran url_verifier on the PDF with a generic token ('EGAS') to confirm it is still live: OK/200. Note the automated PASS the worklist recorded for Length/Diameter ('expected content present') is a weaker signal than it looks -- it is a raw-digit-string match ('14', '12') anywhere in a 36-page report's extracted text, not a check that those digits describe this pipeline. My visual read of the map is the real basis for confirming these two values, not that automated check.

DUPLICATE: checked against the full 40-row roster. P8032 'Ameriya-Dahshour Gas Pipeline' (32in, 200km, endpoint Giza) and P8075 'Western Desert Gas Complex-Ameriya Gas Pipeline (Pipeline 3)' (24in, 26km) are both different diameters and different lengths from this 12in/14km line, and the map shows P8075's likely corridor as the separate 24" 26km W.D.G.-Complex-to-Borg-Elarab-junction line drawn just above/beside this one on the same map -- different diameter is GEM's own stated rule of thumb for 'two real parallel lines, not a duplicate.' Separately, the sheet's own RouteNotes (RouteCreator CB, dated from the 2026-08-10 Egypt-gas route-creation pass) already ran this exact duplicate check against P6032 'Borg El Arab-Midor Gas pipeline' (24in/10km, terminus = Midor refinery, not Amreyah Cement) and reached the same conclusion: distinct, non-duplicate, geographically-nearby laterals feeding the same industrial corridor. I found no reason to disturb that finding.

SECOND-SOURCE EFFORT (existence of the PIPELINE specifically, not just the endpoints): this Claude Code session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) before this row was assigned, and every alternative search surface I tried through WebFetch (Bing, Google, DuckDuckGo HTML/lite, Marginalia) returned CAPTCHA walls, empty template pages, or results for an unrelated cached query -- none returned real SERPs. Within that constraint I fetched two specific candidate corroborators directly: amreyahcement.com/about (the cement company's own site: confirms the plant is real, 5.5 Mt/y capacity, sited at 'Kilo 55, Alexandria-Matrouh North Coast Road') and cemnet.com/global-cement-report/facility/amreyah (independent trade directory: locates the plant in 'Burg al Arab, Alexandria'). Both are genuinely independent of GEM and of each other, and both corroborate that the two named places on this GEM row (Amreyah/Ameriya Cement plant; Borg El Arab) are real and in the stated relative geography -- but neither source names a gas pipeline between them, so they corroborate the ENDPOINTS, not the LINE. Net result: the pipeline's existence and its exact spec (12in/14km) rest on ONE primary, authoritative source (EGAS/GASCO's own official national-grid map) rather than two independent sources describing the pipeline itself -- tier is medium, not high, and I could not clear it to high despite a genuine search effort. This is not a GEM-derived value (GASCO drew this map independently of GEM) and the source does actually depict this specific line by name and spec, so this is a caveat on sourcing depth, not an existence concern.

ATTRIBUTION/CLASSIFICATION/LOCATION: StartState/Province and EndState/Province = Alexandria is correct (Borg El Arab is administratively part of Alexandria Governorate; Amreyah Cement's Kilo 55 site is also within it). EndLocation is blank while EndPrefecture/District carries 'Borg El Arab' -- consistent with the prior route creator's finding that no more specific named facility exists for this endpoint (it is the town's gas take-off point, not a single plant); leaving it blank rather than fabricating a facility name is correct and I am not forcing a fill there. PipelineType=transmission is a reasonable read of GASCO's own map, which draws this line with the same 'Existing P/L' symbology used for unambiguous trunk lines elsewhere on the same map; nothing suggests it should instead be a gathering/process line.

summary: P8031 confirmed (caveat): the cited EGAS/GASCO 2018 map (read visually, p.35) shows an exact 12in/14km 'Ameriya Cement'-'Borg Elarab' existing line matching every sheet value; ruled out as a duplicate of both P8032/P8075 (different diameters) and P6032 (per prior RouteNotes). No UNRESOLVED items; sole caveat is single-source depth for the pipeline itself (endpoints independently corroborated via amreyahcement.com + cemnet.com, but neither names the line) -- tier medium, not high.
